result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A pads the measured values with invented zeros (3.00, 8.000, 41.000), which claims precision that was never recorded. It also adds derived columns and has an empty or clipped '($)' column at the right edge. B shows the values exactly as given and keeps prices at two decimals, but its measured columns are flush-right with different decimal lengths, so the decimals don't stack. B also adds a total, derived columns and heavy bar shading, so overall it is narrowly better on data fidelity. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): A shows every measurement as recorded, with no invented trailing zeros, and formats prices consistently as $XX.XX. Its numbers are right-aligned with units in the cells, so the decimal points don't line up, and it adds derived columns, a total and highlight cards. B lines up the decimals only by padding values with fake precision (3.00, 8.000, 41.000), which breaks the core rubric item; it also adds derived columns and has a clipped '($)' column at the right edge.
